title: Palindrome Partitioning
prompt:
Partition string `s` so that every substring is a palindrome, and return all possible partitionings.

**Example**: `"aab"` → `[["a","a","b"],["aa","b"]]`.

Backtracking: at each start position, try every prefix that is a palindrome, then recurse on the remainder.
hints: From index `start`, try each end so the substring `s[start..end)` is a palindrome.
If it's a palindrome, add it to the path and recurse from `end`; base case is `start == s.length()`.
A simple two-pointer check tells you if a substring is a palindrome.

solution.explanation: Each recursion level commits to one palindromic prefix and delegates the rest — so the choices along a path concatenate back to `s` in order (which is why the pieces' order matters and we compare 'unordered' only at the outer list). Backtracking undoes each prefix to try the next longer one.
